summary: Discusses why the IP6.ARPA DNS zone needs delegation and specifies a plan for operating it. It was replaced by RFC 3596.

plainLanguage.summary: IPv6 needs DNS names for reverse lookup of addresses. RFC 3152 describes delegating the IP6.ARPA zone and deprecates the older IP6.INT usage.

subtitle: Describes delegation of the IP6.ARPA zone for IPv6 reverse mapping.

tldr.problem: IPv6 needed reverse mapping from addresses to DNS names, and documents referred to the older IP6.INT name.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC requests delegation of IP6.ARPA and further delegation to regional IP registries in line with IPv6 address-space assignments.
tldr.outcome: It deprecated IP6.INT references and was obsoleted by RFC 3596.

today: RFC 3152 is a Best Current Practice that was obsoleted by RFC 3596. It updated RFCs 1886, 2553, 2766, 2772 and 2874.

sections.title: Why IP6.ARPA Is Used
sections.content:
IPv6 needs reverse mapping of addresses to DNS names, analogous to the mapping provided by IN-ADDR.ARPA for IPv4. The IAB recommended using the ARPA top-level domain for technical infrastructure subdomains when possible.

IETF consensus had selected IP6.ARPA for mapping IPv6 addresses to DNS names. The zone would be delegated and its names further delegated to regional IP registries.
sections.plainLanguage: Reverse mapping looks up a DNS name from an IP address. The RFC sets out the IP6.ARPA zone for that purpose in IPv6.

sections.title: Deprecating IP6.INT
sections.content:
The RFC deprecates references to IP6.INT in sections of RFCs 1886, 2553, 2766, 2772 and 2874. It defines deprecate to mean the old usage is not appropriate for new implementations and IP6.INT will likely be phased out in an orderly fashion.

The work-unit metadata records that RFC 3152 updates those five RFCs.
sections.plainLanguage: New implementations should not use the old IP6.INT form. The RFC expects it to be phased out in an orderly way.

sections.title: Delegation and Security
sections.content:
The memo requests that IANA delegate IP6.ARPA following instructions from the IAB. Names within the zone are to be delegated to regional IP registries in line with their IPv6 address-space assignments, using a hierarchy that follows those assignments.

The RFC says DNS spoofing of address-to-name mappings has been exploited in IPv4, but it says delegation of IP6.ARPA creates no new Internet security threats.
sections.plainLanguage: The zone is divided further according to IPv6 address assignments. The RFC says the delegation itself adds no new security threats.

references.text: Thomson, S. and C. Huitema, "DNS Extensions to support IP version 6", RFC 1886, December 1995.
Crawford, M. and C. Huitema, "DNS Extensions to Support IPv6 Address Aggregation and Renumbering", RFC 2874, July 2001.
